messages.subject: ddply rescaler inside a function
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use ddply / rescaler inside a function, but it does not
work.

library(plyr)
library(reshape)

# Generate some data
set.seed(321)
myD <- data.frame( Place = sample(c("AWQ","DFR", "WEQ"), 10,
replace=T),
Light = sample(LETTERS[1:2], 15, replace=T),
value=rnorm(30) )

myD1 <- ddply(myD, .(Place, Light), transform,
rng = rescaler(value, type = "range"))

# Ok, works fine
myD1

# But using ddply inside a function does not work
myfunc <- function(xdf, sctype) {
out <- ddply(xdf, .(Place, Light), transform,
rng = rescaler(value, type = sctype))
return(out)
}

myfunc(myD, "range")

>Fehler in switch(type, rank = rank(x, ...), var = , sd = (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))/sd(x, :
> Objekt 'sctype' nicht gefunden

Any ideas on this?

Thanks for any help
Patrick

messages.author: 223beb57ce203bde
messages.subject: Re: ddply rescaler inside a function
parts:
you can try to define your own function:
myfunc <- function(xdf, sctype) {
out <- ddply(xdf, .(Place, Light), function(df){df$rng <-
rescaler(df$value, type=sctype); df})
return(out)
}

Or if you prefer transform, store sctype in your data frame:
myfunc <- function(xdf, sctype) {
xdf$sctype <- sctype;

rng = rescaler(value, type = sctype[1]))
return(out)
}

Ok, the following are completely guessing.
The problem seems to be that rescaler is only looking for sctype in
the data frame and global environment, not the "local environment" for
the function. Probably because the transform function did not pass
that local environment to rescaler?

I think a better solution than mine should try to force rescaler to
search "harder"?

Xie Chao

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: ddply rescaler inside a function
parts:
> Ok, the following are completely guessing.
> The problem seems to be that rescaler is only looking for sctype in
> the data frame and global environment, not the "local environment" for
> the function. Probably because the transform function did not pass
> that local environment to rescaler?

I think the problem is with transform, not with rescaler. If you look
at the source code to transform, you'll see it's evaluating in the
context of parent.frame(). Because transform is activated inside
llply, the parent.frame points to the wrong place and it can't find
sctype. I think the correct way to fix this is to evaluate in the
function in the parent.frame of ddply, but this will take quite a bit
of rewiring. I've added it to my to do list
(http://github.com/hadley/plyr/issues/issue/3), but it might be a
while before I can get around to implementing it

Hadley
